title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 76 (Public deposits by eligible companies)

content.overview: Section 76 permits only an eligible public company to accept deposits from persons other than its members, subject to section 73(2) and the prescribed rules. Under the current rules, eligibility generally requires net worth of at least ₹100 crore or turnover of at least ₹500 crore, plus the required prior shareholder resolution and Registrar filing before public invitation.

content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 76 (Acceptance of deposits from public by certain companies). A public company meeting the prescribed net-worth or turnover threshold may accept deposits from persons other than its members only subject to the requirements of section 73(2) and the applicable rules. Under the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014, an eligible company generally has net worth of at least ₹100 crore or turnover of at least ₹500 crore. The rules also require prior consent by special resolution and filing of that resolution with the Registrar before invitation; where deposits are within the limits specified under section 180(1)(c), an ordinary resolution may suffice. Apply the current rules on credit rating, deposit limits, repayment defaults, security and other prescribed conditions. Section 76 eligibility is distinct from the offence/penalty provisions in section 76A. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Eligible public company
sections.body: Section 76 applies to a public company meeting the prescribed net-worth or turnover criteria. Under the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014, the general threshold is net worth of at least ₹100 crore or turnover of at least ₹500 crore.

sections.heading: Conditions before public invitation
sections.body: The eligible company must comply with section 73(2) and the applicable rules. The rules require prior consent by special resolution and filing of that resolution with the Registrar before invitation to the public. If deposits are within the limits specified under section 180(1)(c), an ordinary resolution may suffice.

sections.heading: Additional safeguards
sections.body: Check the current rules governing credit rating, deposit limits, repayment defaults, security and other prescribed conditions before concluding that a public deposit is permitted.

sections.heading: Separate penalty provision
sections.body: Section 76 identifies eligibility and conditions for public deposits. Section 76A separately addresses punishment for contravention; do not treat the two sections as interchangeable.

hypotheticals.question: A public company has net worth of ₹120 crore and seeks to accept deposits from persons other than its members. Is the net-worth threshold alone sufficient?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Check the other statutory and rule requirements, including section 73(2), prior shareholder resolution and filing with the Registrar before invitation, and current rules on rating, limits, defaults and security.

hypotheticals.question: An eligible public company plans to accept deposits within the limits under section 180(1)(c). What resolution rule may apply?
hypotheticals.analysis: Under the applicable deposit rules, an ordinary resolution may suffice for deposits within the limits specified under section 180(1)(c); otherwise the prior special-resolution requirement must be checked.

distinctions.title: Public-deposit eligibility and contravention penalty
distinctions.left: Section 76 and the deposit rules determine which public companies may accept public deposits and under what conditions.
distinctions.right: Section 76A separately sets consequences for contravention.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming every public company may accept public deposits.
misconceptions.correction: Section 76 is limited to eligible public companies meeting the prescribed threshold and conditions.

misconceptions.trap: Treating the prescribed net-worth/turnover threshold as the only condition.
misconceptions.correction: Section 73(2) and the applicable deposit rules impose additional requirements, including resolution and filing requirements.

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 76 itself as the penalty provision.
misconceptions.correction: Section 76 governs eligibility/conditions; section 76A separately addresses punishment for contravention.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 76 require?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: A public company meeting the prescribed net worth or turnover may accept deposits from the public subject to section 73 conditions and the additional rules.
